speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights): Mr Speaker, Sir, libraries have been an integral part of civilisation throughout history and most definitely an integral part of our lives.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Libraries are not mere buildings with shelves of books.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: From the Library of Alexandria in antiquity to Singapore’s National Library today, libraries have served as enduring institutions for the preservation of knowledge and the advancement of society.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Civilisations rise when they record, preserve and share knowledge.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The act of collecting stories, ideas and discoveries, and making them accessible, has been at the core of humanity’s advancement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Libraries have carried wisdom across centuries and borders.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: They embody the conviction that knowledge should be shared with the many.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: For a nation, libraries are more than cultural symbols.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In Singapore, where our greatest resource is our people, libraries play a role in nurturing our human capital.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Our libraries have supported lifelong learning, from children discovering their first storybook to adults picking up new knowledge and skills.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: They have anchored national literacy campaigns, strengthened education and provided safe and open spaces for learning.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In an era where information can be overwhelming and sometimes misleading, libraries equip citizens with the ability to discern, to think critically, and to engage responsibly in civic life.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Libraries in our community, beyond civilisation and progress, libraries are also about community.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In Singapore, our libraries are not silent monuments.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: They are vibrant living spaces, where neighbours and friends meet, where students study, where seniors gather for talks and where families come together.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Libraries provide not just access to information, but access to one another.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: They embody inclusiveness, anyone can step in freely.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In a world of growing divisions, libraries remain one of the most welcoming spaces in society.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Libraries are also a safe and nurturing space for children within the community.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: A friend of mine, Ervin Yeo, shared with me that he grew up in the Geylang East Library, which is situated in MacPherson.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: When he was a little boy, his grandmother, who was also his caregiver, would leave him there while she went about her daily chores and he would roam the library, freely access the wide range of books available and soak in the wisdom that the books offered.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Growing up in such an environment must have shaped his affable personality and sharp intellect.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: He later became a scholar and, today, he is a highly successful senior corporate leader.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: More recently, a few of my residents, who are young parents of children with special needs, shared with me that the Geylang East Library have been a safe haven for their children.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: When they are busy at work, they find it most reassuring when they know that their children are in the safe bounds of the library with their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: They know that it is a safe space that can help their children learn and grow, that does not judge but embraces all their uniqueness.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Libraries are also a social space for seniors to stay connected with friends and new knowledge.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Again, at the Geylang East Library, we have many seniors who enjoy the access to a wide range of newspapers, publications and an environment where they feel familiar and comfortable.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Apart from meeting like-minded friends from the neighbourhood, they could also participate in the talks, workshops and experience sessions that the library offers.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The library and what it offers give them a reason to look forward to each new day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Our libraries have never stood still, from card catalogues to digital search, from physical shelves to e-books and online databases, from quiet reading rooms to hubs of creativity, where makerspaces, storytelling corners, and digital labs now flourish.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I still remember the days when I had to buy a cashcard to photocopy many, many pages of books so that I can go home and do my project work or paper.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Today, we can easily access the material needed digitally.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, our libraries have evolved with the times.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And in the future, libraries can evolve even further.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Changing lifestyles, evolving reading patterns and ongoing digitalisation are some of the key drivers of how we access and consume knowledge.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As such, I understand that our libraries, from its form, location, to service delivery, will have to adapt as well.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: These residents have deep emotional attachments to the library, many of whom grew up with the library.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Some enjoy bringing their children to the library as it is a safe space for their young ones to hang out and stay engaged meaningfully.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Some have senior parents who see it as a daily routine to go the library to read, socialise and stay active.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: To them, the building is more than a physical icon in MacPherson, but a huge part of their memories, our collective memories.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: To learn of the relocation, we all feel a deep sense of loss.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: According to NLB, there are some reasons that they have considered to make this decision.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, the above three reasons were what I have learnt from NLB.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I understand these reasons and the need for NLB to consider different factors and trade-offs.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ultimately, the NLB has a national mission, but they also need to ensure public dollars are well-spent.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Still, I would like to ask the following questions, One, can more data or statistics be shared about how visitorship has trended over the past years for Geylang East Library and indeed, other libraries in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Two, how has overall readership, whether it is via physical loans or digital access, been trending?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Three, in terms of lifetime cost, how much does it cost to maintain a standalone building like the Geylang East one versus co-locating it in a shopping mall?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Four, if Geylang East Library has to really must be relocated, what will the NLB do to ensure that our residents continue to have easy access to not just the publications but also a space where they can feel safe, to learn, grow and stay meaningfully engaged?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: How will the NLB work with our community to achieve this?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Even as our libraries adopt new models and go digital, let us not lose what once brought us joy, the feel of a real book in our hands, the wonder through crowded shelves that sparks imagination and the shared pleasure of coming together to do something meaningful as a community.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: They remind us that civilisation is built not just on technology or trade, but on ideas shared, stories told, and communities formed.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In Singapore, libraries remain vital to our national progress, nurturing our minds, connecting our people and helping us navigate an uncertain world.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We must treasure them, invest in them and ensure that even as they evolve, our people can continue to access our libraries meaningfully and freely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Member has raised several queries which I will address in my response to this Motion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Digital disruption has impacted libraries worldwide as reading habits shift amidst a rise in digital content consumption.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB's latest National Reading Habits Survey confirms this trend.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: And 81% of adults indicated that they like to consume information via videos, compared to 62% who indicated that they like to consume information via hardcopy sources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To remain relevant, libraries will need to adapt and reinvent how they deliver content and services to its citizens.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Given the shifts in the information landscape, NLB is aware that inaction will undermine the fundamental role libraries and archives play as custodians of knowledge.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In today's digital age, libraries play an even more critical role as community institutions whose physical presence fosters a sense of rootedness in community amongst patrons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to develop our libraries and strengthen its mandate as a key community node to foster learning and reading in this digital age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB has seized the opportunity to re-imagine how libraries should look in the digital age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, let me share three key roles of libraries and how NLB will continue to fulfil them to support the reading, learning and discovery needs of our citizens in the digital age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: First, libraries serve as catalysts for reading and lifelong learning, a key goal that NLB has always championed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We want Singaporeans to discover, or rediscover, their love for reading, be it turning the pages of a physical book or scrolling through an e-book.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond championing a culture of reading, NLB is transforming into a national platform for lifelong learning, working with like-minded partners to provide learning opportunities for everyone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While our libraries have traditionally been successful at engaging children, we have increased our offerings for adults.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB has partnered with SkillsFuture Singapore to help working adults embrace lifelong learning through THRIVE@libraries, our marquee learning festival.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Moreover, learning engagement has been extended to seniors through programmes like Time of Your Life Celebration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To support our Smart Nation ambitions, NLB has invested in initiatives to give citizens opportunities to explore emerging technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One such initiative is StoryGen, which taps on generative artificial intelligence's image generation capabilities to bring stories to life for library patrons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As new technologies emerge, NLB is committed to ensure that these learning opportunities remain accessible for all.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Citizens can count on the public libraries to be a place for them to learn as well as experience new technologies and find out for themselves how exciting these developments can be and how they may apply to everyday life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As libraries empower people to embrace new technologies, libraries will also equip citizens with the skills to go online safely and responsibly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some of you would be familiar with NLB's S.U.R.E. campaign, which stands for Source, Understand, Research, Evaluate, and how it provides everyone with a simple and intuitive framework to assess the reliability of information.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is supported by a range of programmes and resources on topics such as generative artificial intelligence, online scams and digital safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Another area in which libraries have curated resources on is parenting in a digital age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is a challenging experience for many parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Those of us who are parents today did not grow up with digital technologies and are naturally not confident in our ability to guide our children's digital habits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To support digital parenting, NLB has curated relevant resources, such as videos via its LearnX platform, for parents to help their children develop and practise healthy digital habits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB will do more in this area and is conducting parenting programmes and workshops at libraries to help parents and children practise healthy digital habits together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Next, our libraries play an important role in bringing learning and knowledge to those with less means in our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In particular, NLB has been re-inventing itself and its spaces for persons with disabilities (PwDs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In 2023, NLB launched a suite of services for PwDs at the Punggol Library.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This includes Calm Pods, which offer a private and calming sensorial experience to those who might need it, and the Borrow-N-Go tunnel, which enables users to go through the wide passageway and have their books automatically checked out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To ensure that these services are developed to meet the diverse needs of PwDs, NLB had engaged over 500 PwDs and their caregivers to understand how its libraries could better serve their needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As a key social equaliser, NLB continues to support lower-income families through the kidsREAD programme, which promotes reading among young children since 2004.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB launched kidsREAD@Home last year to bring volunteers directly to public rental flats to conduct reading sessions for children, after a pilot in 2023.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To date, almost 200 children have benefited from kidsREAD@Home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They are places where Singaporeans foster connections and encourage one another to learn and discover.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Libraries are spaces where people can discover their interests and connect with like-minded individuals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our libraries are home to 130 volunteer-led learning communities that cover a diverse range of interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some examples include Learning I.T. for Seniors, which is conducted in English and Mandarin, and the Ilham Pustaka Malay Reading Club, which is co-facilitated by established local authors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through these avenues of peer learning, library patrons can exchange knowledge on various interests, generate support for new passion projects and strengthen community networks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond fostering present-day connections, our archives also connect us with our past.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The National Library and National Archives are the memory institutions of Singapore, preserving our documentary heritage and sharing stories of our past that help us have a richer understanding of what it means to be Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The recently launched SG60 Heart&Soul Experience draws extensively from the National Archives' rich repositories of photographs, videos and oral histories, enabling Singaporeans to connect to stories of the past, even as we look towards the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As part of this plan, NLB's strategy has been to move standalone libraries to places which enjoy easy access to transportation hubs and networks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We understand that some Members are concerned about the relocation of the libraries and its impact on the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The decision to relocate any library is not taken lightly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Before deciding to relocate a particular library or to revamp it in-situ, NLB considers various factors, such as land use plans, the number of residents it can best serve, the library's age and the number of years since the last major renovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ultimately, NLB makes the decision based on how it can best serve and reach more patrons with its services and collections.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The upcoming relocation of Geylang East Library to Tanjong Katong Complex, as mentioned by the Member, reflects this approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB had also considered retaining and revamping Geylang East Library at its current location.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We recognise that whenever public libraries are relocated, they will become closer to some residents and farther for others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are thus committed to ensuring that the new locations remain accessible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For residents who live near the existing Geylang East Library, the new location is a short bus ride away.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Notwithstanding this, NLB has engaged Geylang East residents to better understand their needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB is working to identify a potential suitable space nearby to provide some form of library presence, such as a reading corner or a pop-up library.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will also work with relevant grassroots organisations to help residents access NLB's digital resources or delivery services, ensuring continued reading and learning opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our mission is to inspire Singaporeans to read, learn and discover and this mission is stronger than ever.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At the National Day Rally, Prime Minister Wong said that Singapore must be a "we first" society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This aligns with how we envision our libraries, as trusted spaces where people from all walks of life come together as one community to read, learn and discover together.
